$comment: Wavee base culture — every user-facing UI string. Other cultures override per-key and fall back here. Keys flatten to a `Wavee.Strings` class via FluentGpu.SourceGen (Strings.Detail.Play == "detail.play"); parameterized keys expose a typed format method.

drag.$comment: Drag & drop CAPTIONS: what a drop will do (Add to X, Move into X) and, for a refusal, why it will not. A refusing drop target is TRANSPARENT to the engine (discovery walks past it), so the refusal ones are the only thing that tells the user why a drag was turned away — the drag chip shows them beside its not-allowed glyph.
drag.$comment2: The RESTING verb: what the chip says while the drag is travelling and no target is under the pointer. Most of a gesture is spent in that state, and without it the chip named only the song — so the drag never stated what it was FOR. Superseded per-target by the captions above the moment something accepts, and by a refusal reason when something refuses.
